Conjecture (level-one conservativity). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(\Gamma_0\) consist of old Boolean equations and complete accuracy-one blocks whose inputs are affine in the existing variables. Then every fresh accuracy-one block with inputs affine in the existing variables satisfies \(\mathcal I_D(\Gamma_1)\cap\mathbb F_2[Y]=\mathcal I_D(\Gamma_0)\) for all \(D\). Status: finite evidence only. The Boolean-only base is the degree-exact case; the general case cannot use a coefficient substitution, since the disjunction of three affine forms admits none at degree one, nor degree-exactness, since \(C-AB\) vanishes on the base variety at weighted degree four but needs NS degree six. Any proof must use the base's own level-one structure. The coefficient criterion reduces it to closing the congruence system at degree \(D\) for every rank.

Here \(\Lambda^\alpha(m)=\Lambda_1(s^\alpha m)\) are the moments of the fresh coefficients. This is the raw-coefficient-moment interface that the coupled marginal equations deliberately replace by formal Boolean selectors: (CM-source) fixes selector moments, whereas (FB-dual) leaves every coefficient moment free and couples them by input products. The multiplicative ansatz \(\Lambda^\alpha=\Lambda(\varphi_\alpha\,\cdot)\) with \(\deg\varphi_\alpha\le|\alpha|\) is the substitution route and fails beyond rank two; the rank-three witness shows that the free moments do not always close the gap either. Whether they close it over level-one bases is the conjecture above in dual form.

Rank three and beyond. The disjunction of three affine inputs has no affine coefficient substitution: \((1+g_1)(1+g_2)(1+g_3)\) needs \(r_3\mapsto(1+g_1)(1+g_2)\) of degree two, so the substitution route costs one degree on monomials containing \(r_3\) alone, and in general the prefix-product substitution \(r_j\mapsto\prod_{i<j}(1+g_i)\) gives a third loss bound growing quadratically in \(k\). In the coefficient bookkeeping the missing step is \(g_1g_2g_3Q^\varnothing\equiv0\): the relation \((123)\) has slack three but its useful multiples involve \(Q^{12},Q^{13},Q^{123}\) jointly and do not close at degree \(D\). The explicit rank-three witness shows that no argument can close it in general. For inputs of degree \(\delta\) the coefficient proof gives loss at most \(2(\delta-1)\) at rank two.

Why the planned PHP composition test was not run. The proposed next step was to add a complete first-level affine family and a second-level block to a small PHP base and watch the old window. At \(n\le3\) the functional base is refuted at degree four, below the companion degree of any second-level block, and the one-level theorem's ranges need \(h\ge3\ell\) and \(n\ge2k(D+1)-1\). At feasible sizes every outcome is forced by the small refutation degree, so the test cannot distinguish a PHP-relative mechanism from the total-rank bound. A larger instance needs a sparse elimination method.

Main-route assessment. The first obligation is untouched. The cycle adds one general tool, exact at accuracy one: the coefficient criterion, which turns fresh-block conservativity into a finite system of congruences with explicit slack; the rank-two statement it reproves was already available by substitution. The route needs the PHP-relative composition statement; the criterion is the natural language in which to write what a second-level block requires of the first-level images under the affine weighting, and that is the next mathematical step.

Process assessment. The claim-index search should have preceded the proof draft, since the rank-two statement was already recorded as a normalization lemma; the cheap PHP control ran before designing a large test, which avoided an uninformative computation.

Thus this positive-MOD family is excluded without a low bound on its underlying affine rank: the forms \(a_it+q_i+c_i\) can have arbitrarily large rank through their individual literal coordinates. The shared probe can involve many pigeon rows. Affine blocks and the already handled power-input blocks may coexist with this family: their maps use disjoint new coefficient sets, and the largest degree factor is at most \(p\). This does not cover arbitrary collections of positive-MOD affine forms lacking the shared-probe presentation, or later inputs with unrestricted nonlinear selector dependence.
